subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup be allowed to use a bounded share of the job timeout budget instead of the fixed 60-second pre-runner setup watchdog?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix changes how long a genuinely stuck isolated setup can occupy cron capacity; that is a maintainer product/availability tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the bounded setup budget
options.body: Land PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 so slow but healthy isolated setup can pass the old 60s ceiling while still retaining a cap.

options.title: Require a different cap or knob
options.body: Ask the fix PR to use a lower cap or explicit operator configuration before merging the behavior change.

options.title: Keep the fixed 60s watchdog
options.body: Reject the longer setup window and instead direct affected deployments to reduce cron concurrency, change models, or use command cron where applicable.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded setup budget
recommendation.body: Land PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 so slow but healthy isolated setup can pass the old 60s ceiling while still retaining a cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete authored the earlier watchdog diagnostics and timer-helper owner boundary, making him the strongest history-backed decision owner for this tradeoff.
